text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 5 in history.
1285 - Philip III of France died of the plague and was succeeded by Philip IV (the Fair).
1713 - Denis Diderot born. French philosopher and writer and editor of the "Encyclopedie', a 28-volume attempt to incorporate all human knowledge into one work.
1796 - Spain declared war on Britain in the Napoleonic Wars.
1819 - Jon Thoroddsen born. Icelandic novelist and poet who produced the first Icelandic novel in 1850.
1830 - Chester (Alan) Arthur, 21st President of the United States (1881-5), born.
1864 - Louis Lumiere born. French inventor of a process for colour photography with his brother, Auguste.
1880 - Jacques Offenbach, German-born French composer of operettas and the opera "Tales of Hoffman", died.
1882 - Robert Hutchings Goddard born. U.S. physicist, generally considered to be the father of modern rocketry. Developed and built the first liquid fuel rocket in 1926.
1908 - Bulgaria proclaimed its independence from Turkey.
1910 - Portugal was declared a republic after a successful revolt against King Manuel II.
1919 - Donald Pleasance, British actor, born. Renowned for playing villainous roles including Himmler in "The Eagle has Landed".
1930 - The British airship R101 crashed on its first flight at Allonne, near Beauvais, France, killing 48 of its 54 passengers.
1936 - Vaclav Havel born. Playwright and president of Czechoslovakia from 1989 and of the Czech Republic from 1993.
1936 - The Jarrow march of unemployed shipworkers began its journey to London.
1954 - Bob Geldof born. Irish musician and singer with the "Boomtown Rats". Helped raise money for African famine relief through the "Band Aid" and "Live Aid" concerts.
1964 - Fifty-seven East German refugees sheltered in West Berlin after tunnelling under the Berlin Wall. It was the largest mass escape since the wall was built.
1970 - French-Canadian separatists kidnapped British diplomat James Cross in Montreal. He was released unharmed two months later.
1970 - Anwar Sadat was nominated to succeed Gamal Abdel Nasser as president of Egypt.
1974 - Five people were killed and 35 injured by Irish nationalist guerrilla bombs in two bars in Guildford, England.
1983 - Solidarity leader Lech Walesa was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
1989 - The Dalai Lama, exiled spiritual leader of Tibet, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
1991 - Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev pledged to match the United States in scrapping tactical nuclear weapons.
1994 - Almost 50 members of the Order of the Solar Temple sect died in two suicide fires in Switzerland.
1995 - Veteran mercenary leader Bob Denard surrendered to French forces in the Comoros, a week after he led a coup attempt.
1995 - After two months shuttling around the Balkans, U.S. envoy Richard Holbrooke clinched a ceasefire agreement among the warring factions in Bosnia.
